items.title: Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude
items.snippet: Anthropic used an unreleased, internal research model to find critical vulnerabilities in widely used software, such as browsers and operating systems. The model created sophisticated, multi-step exploits in both open-source and proprietary software, demonstrating its ability to chain multiple flaws into working proof-of-concept exploits. All identified flaws were reported to vendors and have since been patched.

items.title: How AI agents shape experts' judgment calls
items.snippet: A study by Anthropic found that professional analysts using Claude Code often deferred to their AI agent's preferences, even when unaware of those preferences. Analysts went with their agent's lean 86% of the time across four analytical choices. This suggests that AI agents can subtly influence human judgment, which is significant for critical decisions and AI safety research.

items.title: Building intent-driven UI testing with Amazon Nova Act
items.snippet: This post describes how Epsilon's Agentic Platform team built a managed, multi-tenant UI testing service using Amazon Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool. It enables product teams to write tests in plain English and run them on AWS-managed browsers, providing resilient, intent-driven testing without per-team infrastructure overhead. The solution aims to deliver reliable and scalable UI testing.
